items.canonical_answer: Genotype is the genetic make-up of an organism in terms of the alleles present.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the definition: the genetic make-up of an organism.
1 mark: the key feature it must include: in terms of the alleles present.

items.prompt: For a plant in which tall (T) is dominant to short (t), a learner records a cross only as "tall × short". Explain why this does not specify both parental genotypes.
items.canonical_answer: Tall and short describe phenotypes, not pairs of alleles. The short parent is tt, but the tall parent could be TT or Tt, so the record does not identify one genotype pair.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: identifies the error: tall and short are phenotypes, whereas genotypes are written as allele pairs.
1 mark: the short parent must be tt but the tall parent could be TT or Tt, so its genotype is not specified.
items.provenance: Authored for the 6116 structural exemplar from the topic 4 claim ledger.

items.prompt: In a pearl millet variety, the allele for tall stems (T) is dominant to the allele for short stems (t). Two heterozygous tall plants are crossed, and 160 seeds grow into plants. Draw a genetic diagram for this cross, and use it to calculate how many plants are expected to be short.
items.canonical_answer: Parental phenotypes: tall × tall. Parental genotypes: Tt × Tt. Gametes: T, t and T, t. Offspring genotypes: TT, Tt, Tt, tt. Offspring phenotypes: 3 tall : 1 short. Short plants expected: 160 ÷ 4 = 40.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: method: parental phenotypes and genotypes (Tt × Tt) on the diagram.
1 mark: gametes T and t from each parent.
1 mark: all four offspring genotypes, from a grid or lines.
1 mark: final answer: 40 short plants, with working.
items.provenance: Authored for the 6116 structural exemplar from the topic 4 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Two heterozygous tall plants (Tt) are crossed. Explain why about one offspring in four is short, and why a small number of seeds may not show this ratio exactly.
items.canonical_answer: Each parent passes on T or t with equal chance, so one fertilisation in four gives tt, which is short. The ratio is a probability: a small number of offspring can differ from it by chance.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the reason: each parent gives t half the time, so tt is one in four.
1 mark: because the ratio is a probability, small samples differ by chance.

items.prompt:
In a pearl millet variety, the allele for tall stems (T) is dominant to the allele for short stems (t).
(a) State the genotype of a short plant. [1]
(b) Name the phenotype of a plant with the genotype Tt. [1]
(c) Draw a genetic diagram to show a cross between two heterozygous plants. [3]
(d) A farmer near Outapi grows 200 plants from this cross. Calculate how many are expected to be tall. [2]
(e) Suggest why the number of tall plants the farmer counts may differ from your answer to (d). [1]
items.canonical_answer:
(a) tt.
(b) Tall.
(c) Parents: Tt × Tt. Gametes: T and t from each parent. Offspring: TT, Tt, Tt, tt; 3 tall : 1 short.
(d) 200 ÷ 4 = 50 short, so 50 × 3 = 150 tall.
(e) A ratio predicts proportions; the actual offspring can differ from it by chance.
marking_guidance: (c) 3 marks: 1 mark for parental genotypes and gametes; 1 mark for all four offspring genotypes; 1 mark for the 3 : 1 phenotype ratio. Accept a grid in place of lines.
(d) 2 marks: 1 mark for the working (one in four short, or three in four tall); 1 mark for 150.
(e) 1 mark: chance, or a ratio is a prediction, is the creditable point.
